articles.title: Ebola spreads to 60 health zones in eastern DRC; UN warns of funding shortfall
articles.author: Pavan Kulkarni
articles.content_excerpt: The fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history, killing nearly one in two infected in the eastern region of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), has spread to six new health zones between August 14 and August 28. The spread remains within six of the country’s 26 provinces identified before August 14: namely Bas-Uélé, Haut-Uélé, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo. However, the number of health zones affected within these six provinces increased from 54 of the 151 to 60 over the following two weeks. The spread was identified in a new health zone of the Tshopo province on August 15. By August 23, the spread was also confirmed in Viadana in Bas-Uélé and Mutwanga in North Kivu. On August 28, infections were also confirmed in the Ganga health zone of Bas-Uélé as well as in Biena and Man

articles.title: Will a new political alliance unseat the Abbas-led Palestinian Authority?
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: After over two decades of political impasse caused by the division between the major Palestinian factions Fatah and Hamas, a new alliance in the making has revealed itself as a national unity coalition. The coalition will participate in the historic November 28 elections for the Palestinian Legislative Council (PLC). The PLC elections were held in 2006. According to media reports, the emerging election coalition comprises the Fatah-affiliated Democratic Reform Current and led by Mohammad Dahlan, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, the Popular Resistance Committees, and Nasser al-Qudwa’s National Democratic Forum. articles.title: When the mountain broke: inside Nepal’s deadliest Himalayan flood
articles.author: Madhab Pant
articles.content_excerpt: At roughly 8:30 am on August 26, 2026, a wall of water, mud, ice, and massive boulders roared down the Lhende Khola into the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems. The surge struck without local rainfall or warning sirens, catching border communities like Timure, mid-morning. Initial reports mistook the ground tremors for an earthquake, but satellite and seismic data later confirmed the real trigger: a high-altitude collapse of rock and ice near Langtang Lirung, on the Tibetan side, spanning nearly one square kilometer and generating a ground shock equivalent to a magnitude 5.2 quake. articles.title: “Catastrophe of Unimaginable Proportions”: Nepal Flood Death Toll Tops 900; Near 5,000 Still Missing
articles.content_excerpt: More than 900 people in Nepal are confirmed dead after a massive wall of water, mud and debris crashed through a Himalayan river valley on the border with Tibet. More than 4,200 people are missing in Nepal and hundreds more in Tibet. Families are searching hospitals for loved ones, and crews have buried hundreds of unidentified bodies in shallow graves. Rescue efforts are also underway for more than 900 hydropower workers, believed to be trapped in more than a dozen underground tunnels blocked by debris. articles.title: The Real Reason There’s a Munitions Shortage? Too Many Wars & a Dysfunctional Pentagon: William Hartung
articles.content_excerpt: Top U.S. military leaders have reportedly advised Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth against extending the war in Iran because ongoing operations in the Middle East have degraded the Pentagon’s ability to confront threats elsewhere. According to The Washington Post , the warnings appeared in a classified assessment for Hegseth prepared by the heads of the Army, Navy and Air Force, and the four-star commanders overseeing U.S. operations throughout Europe, Asia and Latin America. This comes after multiple reports have revealed the U.S. is facing a critical munitions shortage, having used up much of its global stockpile of expensive missile systems during the war against Iran. “The Pentagon is completely dysfunctional when it comes to fighting this kind of war,” says defense analyst William Hartu

articles.title: “Left Behind and Overlooked”: Indiana Energy Company Left Majority-Black Gary Powerless for Weeks
articles.content_excerpt: Thousands of residents recently spent two weeks without power in Gary, Indiana, following a storm that ripped through the majority-Black city. The blackout ground the city to a halt, trapping residents in their apartments, forcing the closure of many businesses and leading to fuel shortages at gas stations.
